face: I shall remember this little exchange when the council next sits, {player}. Memory is a patient sort of weapon, you know.
Go on, then. Walk away. The rest of the realm will be talking about who blinked first, and I do hope it is not you.
We are finished here, and I suspect the fief will be better governed for it. Try not to trip over your own ambitions on the road.
Mind the bridge at the ford, {player}. It has a habit of collapsing under people who stand too near to my dealings.
A pleasure as always, which is to say not at all. I will draft the minutes of this meeting myself, so you may rest assured of their accuracy.
Good day. I have three letters to write before supper, and at least one of them will concern you and the company you keep.
Off you go. When the vote comes, I expect your absence will be noticed far more than your presence ever was.
Farewell, {player}. Do not bother sending word of the next council. I have already told the others what to expect from you.
Enjoy your walk. I shall be sure to mention your failure to keep your word to {my_faction} at the next gathering, with suitable sorrow.
I think we both know this will not end well for one of us, and I have already made my choice of which one. Good day.
Very well. We shall speak again when there is something worth the time, though I am not yet convinced there will be.
Thank you for your company this afternoon. I will weigh what you said against what others have told me, and then decide what it meant.
Until we meet at the council, I suggest you consider which side of the table you would prefer to sit on. The seating is not yet fixed.
Good day to you. Mind the carts on the east road; they have been blocking traffic since the harvest levies were announced.
We have covered a good deal of ground today. I shall see what the fief elders make of it before I commit to anything further.
Farewell for now. I expect a number of rumours will reach you before sundown, and I would be grateful if you judged them on their merits.
This has been a useful conversation, if not a conclusive one. Let us reconvene once the tithe reports have been read and properly argued over.
Take care on the road. Plenty of people are asking questions about the grain stores this week, and I should hate for you to be caught unawares.
Well, that was civil enough. I will consider your proposal alongside the others on my desk, which is a longer list than you might imagine.
I have other appointments, I am afraid. But do give my regards to whoever it is you are answering to these days, for I have been wondering.
Ah, {player}, you have made my day considerably brighter. We must dine properly soon and perhaps draft something together for the council.
Safe travels, my friend. Keep your ears open in the market; I am certain you will hear something useful for both of us.
Off to the western fiefs, then? Send word of any movements there, and I shall return the favour with everything I learn.
Go with my blessing, though I confess my blessing is always conditional on your continued enthusiasm for our little arrangement.
You are one of the few who truly understands how these things are done. Let us speak again before the next vote, and bring your best ideas.
Another splendid meeting. I shall write to the others tonight and tell them you are the sort of ally they ought to have counted on sooner.
Walk well. Should anyone ask your opinion of me, I trust you will remember that I have been nothing but generous to your interests.
Off you go, then. I have a few quiet words to arrange on your behalf, and I rather enjoy being the one who makes things happen.
It is always a pleasure to speak with someone who sees the realm's future as clearly as you do. Let us keep this partnership quietly in mind.
Farewell, dear friend. Remember that a well-placed favour today is worth a dozen speeches in the council hall next season.
